title: Next Greater Element on a Circle

concept.title: Go around the circle twice
body: The array is **circular**: after the last element comes the first one again. The next greater element of an element may therefore be **before** it in the array, found after wrapping around.

The simplest trick: walk through the indexes **twice**, `i = 0, 1, ..., 2n - 1`, and use `i % n` for the element. Push an index only during the **first** round (so that every element is pushed once); in both rounds, pop waiting elements that are smaller than the current one and give them this value as their answer.
Elements that are still waiting after two rounds have no greater element at all (they are maxima), and keep -1.

statement: The numbers of an array are arranged on a circle (the element after the last one is the first one). For each element, print the first greater element you meet when you go forward around the circle, or -1 if there is none.

examples.note: After 1 comes 2; after 2 nothing is greater (-1); the last 1 wraps around to the first 1, then reaches 2.

hints: Go through the array twice with `i % n`.
Only push indexes during the first round.
Elements still on the stack at the end keep the answer -1.

explanation: Walking around the circle twice lets every element see all others. Indexes are pushed in the first round only; waiting elements are answered by the first greater value in either round.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

res = [-1] * n
stack = []
for i in range(2 * n):
    x = a[i % n]
    while stack and a[stack[-1]] < x:
        res[stack.pop()] = x
    if i < n:
        stack.append(i)
print(*res)
